title: Astrid and the Inventory
premise: Jonah Nystrom, a bridge inspector whose marriage has become a matter of load tolerances and deferred maintenance, is assigned to assess the old ferry crossing in a fading coastal town. There he meets Astrid Vinter, the last fluent speaker of a dying language, who asks him to record her inventory of words before she dies — an inheritance no one else wants. As Jonah learns her tongue, word by word, his wife Marta arrives to confront the stranger she's become to him, and Astrid forces both of them to translate what they've never said aloud. When Astrid dies mid-lesson, Jonah must choose between returning to the marriage he merely inhabits or becoming the owner of a life he finally understands; he stays, teaches the language to a classroom of children, and signs his name — not as a tenant — on the deed of his own days.
about_author: Xanthe Dunmore is the pen name of a former lexicographer who spent a decade cataloguing endangered words for regional archives before turning to fiction. She lives near a decommissioned ferry crossing and writes about the arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He inspects a highway bridge, measuring cracks with calipers while composing a mental inspection report on his own marriage to Marta: hairline fractures, deferred maintenance, no imminent collapse but no margin left. The emotional beat is quiet dread — a man who knows structures better than feelings, sensing failure he cannot yet name.

chapters.title: The Ferry Crossing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Assigned to assess the condemned ferry terminal at Vinter Point, he finds Astrid Vinter, ninety-one, sitting on the rusted ramp watching water. She mistakes him for someone come 'for the words.' He corrects her; she insists he'll be back. The beat is reluctant curiosity — duty pulling him somewhere he didn't plan to go.

chapters.title: A Grammar of Small Things
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with a letter from Marta interspersed. He returns off-schedule; Astrid begins teaching him names for things — tide, gull, rust, grief — explaining that her language has no word for 'own,' only 'keep for now.' He starts recording her on his phone. The beat is awakening: language as a door he didn't know was locked.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Photographs
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Sorting old albums at home, she finds photos of Jonah laughing in ways she hasn't seen in years — from before. She drives to Vinter Point unannounced and watches through a window as her husband leans toward an old woman like a son. The beat is jealous bewilderment: grief for a version of him she thought was gone forever.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Astrid reveals why she needs a student: the town council wants the terminal demolished, and with it the last place her language was spoken daily. Jonah begins transcribing her word-hoard — 4,000 entries — realizing each session costs her strength. The beat is rising stakes: an inheritance with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: What the Word for Leave Means
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. She confronts Jonah at the terminal; their argument spills into Astrid's kitchen, where Astrid interrupts with a single word that means both 'to leave' and 'to let grow.' Forced to sit across from each other, Jonah and Marta say true things for the first time in years. The beat is rupture turning toward honesty.

chapters.title: Load Rating
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. His inspection report recommends demolition, and signing it feels like betrayal; he delays filing, jeopardizing his job. Meanwhile Astrid's health fails — a fall, a hospital stay — and she drills him harder, angry at time. The beat is mounting pressure: every loyalty now demands a sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the hospital, Astrid teaches him the word for 'forgive' — literally, 'to see again clearly' — and makes him recite the photographs' story: not her sins, but his mother's, whom Astrid once taught too. She dies at dawn mid-lesson, one word unfinished. The beat is devastating tenderness; the climax of loss.

chapters.title: Seeing Again
chapters.summary: Marta and Jonah, alternating. At the funeral, Jonah plays the recordings publicly; the town hears its buried tongue and weeps. He files a revised report proposing preservation, resigning when overruled. That night he and Marta read Astrid's notebooks together, translating side by side. The beat is conversion: forgiveness enacted, not just understood.

chapters.title: Keep for Now
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, coda. A year later: the terminal stands as a language school, Jonah teaching children words for tide and gull, Marta running the archive beside him. On the last page of the inventory, Astrid left the unfinished word completed in her own hand — it means 'beginning.' Jonah signs the visitor ledger with his full name. The beat is resolution: ownership, at last, of a life kept for now and given forward.
